$comment: The canonical product categories, and the size run each one sells in.
One file because they are one decision. A category is the thing the price
list names, the thing the card badge and the PDP eyebrow show, and the thing
that determines which sizes a listing carries — and those had drifted apart
before. The catalogue was imported in several lineages that each invented
their own wording, so the same category was live under as many as four names
JSON rather than TypeScript because the offline scripts are plain Node .mjs
and cannot import a .ts module. Both sides read this: client/src/lib/catalog.ts
exports CANONICAL_TYPES and SIZE_RUNS from it for the app and the live smoke
test, and scripts/apply-client-sizing.mjs reads it directly.
Adding a category is a deliberate act. The live smoke test in
server/shopify.smoke.test.ts fails on any productType that is not in this
file, which is what stops an importer reintroducing a spelling.
Size runs are the client's 7 September 2026 price list, which supersedes the
$sizeRunsComment: Kids sizes are ages (2-3 … 10-11) and are set per product at import time from
the batch manifest, so a category whose run is null is never swept by
apply-client-sizing.mjs. Service products carry no size at all.
